samples.summary: `create`'s cross-workspace parent check is only asserted by "the mock was called" — no test proves a rejected parent stops the folder being created
samples.evidence: The only coverage for the parent check in `create` is `it('checks a supplied parent belongs to the route workspace')`, which asserts `expect(folderService.assertSameWorkspace).toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS)` and nothing else. That assertion holds even if the controller dropped the `await` (or ignored a rejection), in which case a folder could be parented under a folder in another workspace. The sibling `documents.controller.spec.ts` does have the corresponding negative case ('refuses a folder from another workspace' → rejects and `updateDocument` not called); the folders spec has no equivalent for `create`: no test mocks `assertSameWorkspace.mockRejectedValue(...)` and asserts `folderService.create` was not called. The v1 folders routes also have no e2e coverage (packages/backend/test/folder.e2e-spec.ts only hits the web routes `/workspaces/:id/folders` and `/folders/:id`), so nothing else exercises this path.
searchedFor: grep '/folders' in packages/backend/test (only web routes found)

samples.summary: New HttpClient methods (folder CRUD, copyDocument, moveDocument) are never exercised; the CLI tests mock HttpClient entirely, so real path/method/body are unverified
samples.evidence: `vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js', ...)` replaces HttpClient with a stub class, so `listFolders`/`createFolder`/`renameFolder`/`moveFolder`/`deleteFolder`/`copyDocument`/`moveDocument` in packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts (their verbs, `/folders` paths, `seg()` escaping and `{parentId}` / `{folderId}` bodies) are never executed by any test. The `--dry-run` assertions pin URLs built by `printDryRun`, a separate code path that duplicates the strings, so a divergence between the preview and the real request (wrong verb, wrong body key) would pass. packages/cli/test/http-client-paths.test.ts exercises the real client against a fetch mock but adds no folder/copy/move cases.
searchedFor: glob packages/cli/test/*.ts for a folders/http-client test

samples.summary: `remove` has no test for the folder author deleting their own folder — the author branch of the manager check is untested for delete
samples.evidence: The `remove` describe covers: plain member forbidden, workspace owner allowed, owner-minted API key allowed, demoted-minter key forbidden, minter-left forbidden. There is no case with `req(AUTHOR)` against a folder whose `authorID` is AUTHOR, so the `isDocumentManager(role, folder.authorID, userId)` author path in `remove` (folders.controller.ts:148) is only covered via `update`. If the author branch regressed for delete, an author would be unable to delete their own folder and no test would fail.
searchedFor: read the full remove describe in folders.controller.spec.ts
grep for req(AUTHOR) usages in that spec

samples.summary: Folder `update` has no test that a rejected `assertSameWorkspace` blocks the write, and none combining name + parentId in one call
samples.evidence: 'checks the new parent for workspace and cycles before writing' makes `assertNoCycle` reject and asserts `assertSameWorkspace` was merely called; no test makes `assertSameWorkspace` itself reject and asserts `folderService.update` was not called (the documents spec does have that case). samples.summary: Nothing tests that ApiV1FoldersController is actually registered/DI-resolvable in ApiV1Module
samples.evidence: The new controller's specs instantiate it with `new ApiV1FoldersController(mock, mock)` and the guard checks read class metadata, so both pass whether or not the controller is in `ApiV1Module.controllers` and whether or not `FolderService`/`WorkspaceService` resolve at boot. A grep for `ApiV1FoldersController` finds only api-v1.module.ts, the controller, its spec and the write-scope guard spec — no module compilation/e2e test. Same for the newly injected `DocumentCopyService` on the documents controller (DocumentModule does export it, so DI is in fact fine, but no test asserts it).

samples.summary: No test for an API-key request whose `user.id` is absent, where `Number(user.id)` becomes NaN in the new assertMember call
samples.evidence: The new API-key branch calls `assertMember(resolvedWorkspaceId, Number(user.id))`. Both new tests pass `{ id: 7, isApiKey: true }`; the pre-existing 'forbids an API key scoped to a different workspace' test passes a user with no `id`, but it returns before the membership check. No test covers an in-scope key with a missing/non-numeric id, so a NaN lookup (which would silently depend on `assertMember`'s behaviour) is unexercised.

samples.summary: The removeMember revocation test asserts `$transaction` was called but cannot show the two writes are atomic, and does not assert the membership delete itself
samples.evidence: The mock `$transaction` invokes the callback with the same prisma mock, so the test proves ordering/atomicity of nothing; it asserts `apiKey.updateMany` args and `expect(prisma.$transaction).toHaveBeenCalled()`. The new test also never asserts `workspaceMember.delete` was called with the right composite key inside the transaction. This is a limit of unit-testing a transaction rather than a wrong test, and the where-clause assertion (workspaceId + createdBy + revokedAt) is meaningful.
searchedFor: read workspace.service.spec.ts removeMember describe and createMockPrisma

mergedFrom.summary: Folder `update` has no test that a rejected `assertSameWorkspace` blocks the write, and none combining name + parentId in one call
mergedFrom.evidence: 'checks the new parent for workspace and cycles before writing' makes `assertNoCycle` reject and asserts `assertSameWorkspace` was merely called; no test makes `assertSameWorkspace` itself reject and asserts `folderService.update` was not called (the documents spec does have that case). verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `create` (folders.controller.ts:88-105) enforces the cross-workspace parent rule solely by awaiting `assertSameWorkspace`, and the only test covering it (folders.controller.spec.ts:92-95) asserts nothing but `toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS)`. `assertSameWorkspace` is mocked resolved in beforeEach (line 67) and never re-mocked to reject for `create`, so no test shows a rejected parent stops `folderService.create`. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: no v1 folders e2e coverage (folder.e2e-spec.ts hits only the web routes; `api/v1` in packages/backend/test appears only for documents paths), the CLI folders tests mock the HTTP layer, `api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:69` only checks guard metadata, and there is no folder.service spec. The sibling negative cases exist for documents (documents.controller.spec.ts:216) and files (files.controller.spec.ts:263), confirming the folders gap is a genuine omission of a cross-tenant write guard's enforcement test — major under this lens.

searchedFor: checked packages/backend/src/document/document.dto.spec.ts pattern for a documents PATCH DTO spec
finding.summary: No test that PATCH /documents/:id now drops unknown body fields (mass-assignment regression would be invisible)
finding.evidence: The diff replaces `data: body` (the whole request body spread straight into `prisma.document.update`) with an explicit whitelist building `Prisma.DocumentUpdateInput` from `title` and `folderId` only (documents.controller.ts, `update`). The handler takes an inline `@Body() body: { title?; folderId? }`, not a DTO class, so the global `ValidationPipe({whitelist:true})` in main.ts:66 cannot strip anything — the controller whitelist is the only protection. Every new `update` test in documents.controller.spec.ts passes only `title` and/or `folderId` (lines 177-254); none sends an extra field such as `authorID`, `workspaceId`, `type` or `fileId` and asserts it is absent from the `updateDocument` argument. A future edit reverting to a spread, or adding a field to the loop, would keep the whole suite green while letting an API-key caller rewrite document ownership/workspace.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. documents.controller.spec.ts:262-277 ('drops unknown body fields instead of writing them') sends title plus the exact fields the finding names — type, authorID, workspaceId, fileId, id — cast `as never` past the inline body type, and asserts updateDocument was called with `{ where: { id: 'doc-1' }, data: { title: 'New' } }`. Because toHaveBeenCalledWith is a deep-equality match, any leaked key fails it, so a revert to `data: body` would turn this test red. A second case at documents.controller.spec.ts:279-288 sends only unknown fields and asserts `data: {}`. Both drive the real controller whitelist at documents.controller.ts:122-155 with only collaborator services mocked, so the logic under test is not mocked away. The reviewer's description of the production code is correct, but the assertion that no test sends an extra field is contradicted by the file: their cited window ended at line 254 and the two mass-assignment tests begin at 256, prefaced by a comment stating they are the cases that would fail if the spread returned.

finding.summary: Nothing asserts CombinedAuthGuard/WorkspaceScopeGuard are mounted on the new folders controller, and its list/create handlers do no workspace check of their own
finding.evidence: `ApiV1FoldersController.list` (folders.controller.ts:107-110) and `create` (88-105) trust the route `workspaceId` outright — the only thing refusing an API key minted for another workspace is the class-level `@UseGuards(CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard)`. folders.controller.spec.ts instantiates the controller with `new ApiV1FoldersController(...)`, so guards never run there, and the only guard-mounting test added (api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:64-78) asserts solely that `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` is in `__guards__` — it does not check `WorkspaceScopeGuard`. So dropping or reordering that guard would leak/allow writes to another workspace's folder tree with the whole suite green. No e2e covers the new surface either (packages/backend/test/folder.e2e-spec.ts exercises only the web `folders/:id` routes; grep for 'api/v1' in it finds nothing).

verdict.reason: The finding claims nothing asserts that CombinedAuthGuard/WorkspaceScopeGuard are mounted on ApiV1FoldersController. folders.controller.spec.ts opens with a `describe('ApiV1FoldersController guards')` block (lines 13-36) that reads `Reflect.getMetadata('__guards__', ApiV1FoldersController)` and asserts with `it.each` that CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard AND ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard are each in that list (`expect(guards).toContain(guard)`, lines 20-26), plus an ordering assertion that CombinedAuthGuard precedes WorkspaceScopeGuard (lines 31-35). '__guards__' is precisely the metadata key Nest's @UseGuards writes, and it matches the decorator at folders.controller.ts:38-39. Removing or reordering WorkspaceScopeGuard would turn the suite red, which is the exact failure mode the finding says would go undetected. The spec even documents the reasoning (lines 7-12): the handlers trust the route workspaceId, guards do not run under direct instantiation, so the mounting metadata is asserted instead. One counterexample is enough for an absence claim; the secondary points about api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts and the missing e2e do not revive it because the named risk (dropped/reordered guard) is covered.
